title: Profiled service lanes PRD and cutover playbook
creator: Maya Gonzalez
background: Teams building customer-facing features need predictable latency/cost/quality tradeoffs. The hosted endpoints currently expose a single behavior per route; that forces product teams to choose between higher-cost stable output or lower-cost capacity-optimized variants. This PRD defines 'profiled service lanes' (low-latency, standard, cost-optimized) to let tenants select per-request behavior without breaking the API.
goal: Ship a testable, documented profiled tiers surface across chat, completions, embeddings and rerank endpoints; provide canary and beta gating so customers can opt in safely.
success_metrics: Adoption: >= 10 paying tenants using profiles within 6 weeks of GA
Cost delta: Cost-optimized profile reduces per-token unit cost by >= 25% for compatible workloads
Reliability: No increase in P95 end-to-end error rate during canary: <= baseline + 0.5% absolute
Support: Fewer than 5 quality-regression support tickets in the first 30 days post-GA
requirements: API: Add a 'profile' query parameter and 'X-Redwood-Profile' header accepted by chat, completions, embeddings and rerank; default when omitted = 'standard'
Console: Per-endpoint UI to set tenant-default profile and preview estimated cost/latency/quality tradeoffs before enabling
Runtime: Request-time mapping that selects model variant, batching window, and quantization target based on profile; must be pluggable into smart routing
Billing: Telemetry to attribute usage by profile; cost projection surfaced in Console prior to opt-in
Evals: Automated evaluation harness that runs representative prompts across profiles and outputs quality deltas
Observability: Per-profile traces, token-cost breakdown and SLO dashboards for latency, error-rate and quality samples
Rollout: Canary and beta gating policy with automated rollback when thresholds breached
non_goals: No new model training or fine-tuning workflows in V1; profiles map to existing model variants or runtime configs
Private/on-prem packaging excluded from V1; hosted only at launch
No per-prompt dynamic profile auto-selection in V1; client chooses profile per request
scope_changes: Removed: per-prompt predictive cost estimation from V1 due to infra bandwidth; moved to follow-up PM-468872
Deferred: tenant-customizable profile definitions — V1 ships with fixed profile set only
Deferred: SDK helper that auto-selects profiles — to ship in subsequent SDK release
acceptance_criteria: Contract: 'profile' parameter recognized by chat/completions/embeddings/rerank and default behavior unchanged for clients that omit it
Runtime: Documented mapping for each profile to model variant, batching timeout and quantization target exists and is deployed to staging
Telemetry: Per-profile usage shows in Console usage tables and exports to billing pipeline in staging
Evals: Quality delta report for each profile/endpoint shows no >8% degradation in primary quality metric vs 'standard' without explicit PM signoff
Canary: Internal canary to 3 tenants at 1% traffic each for 72 hours with automated SLO gates and rollback triggers
Docs/SDKs: Public API docs updated and at least one SDK (python or js) includes examples for 'profile' parameter
Ops: Pager and support runbooks updated with profile-specific troubleshooting and rollback steps
Performance: 'low-latency' profile median latency meets documented targets in dedicated hosted regions
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy mappings and telemetry to staging and run smoke tests. 2) Internal canary: 3 internal tenants, 1% slice each for 72 hours. 3) Beta opt-in: up to 20 external tenants for 14 days with monitoring. 4) Self-serve GA: enable Console toggle with consent and cost estimate overlay. 5) Post-GA: 30-day quality review and opt-out support window. Automated rollback on SLO breach; manual rollback via feature flag.
launch_checklist: Console: behind-flag tenant opt-in UI and cost overlay implemented
Runtime: profile-to-variant mapping deployed to staging and smoke-tested
Evals: full eval suite executed and quality thresholds validated
Monitoring: per-profile dashboards and alerts created (latency P95, error-rate, token-cost drift)
SDKs: release python and js SDK patches with migration examples
Billing: billing attribution validated with dry-run invoices for beta tenants
Support: runbook updated and tabletop incident exercise completed
Security: security review completed and signoff recorded
Canary: internal canary executed and metrics green
Beta: selected customers enabled for opt-in and feedback collected
GA: flip Console toggle to GA, publish changelog and customer communications
Post-launch: 30-day quality review scheduled and opt-out process documented
